content.text:
**Finding: T4C — compliant (at fallback, partly above it).**

- **Customer convenience right:** § 17(b) lets Sparkling terminate "at any time" on 90 calendar days' written notice — an unconditional election, within the fallback 60–90 day band.
- **No penalty:** no early-termination fee, penalty or forfeiture anywhere (§ 11 Fees, § 17), so the fallback three-month cap is comfortably beaten.
- **No Vendor convenience right:** § 17(a) keeps the licence perpetual while fees are paid; Garman's only exits are the mutual insolvency/uncured-material-default triggers in § 17(c). The § 10 maintenance term is "renewable" with no Garman discontinuation right. This meets the *preferred* element that Vendor have no mid-term convenience right.
- **Short of preferred only on minor points:** notice is 90 rather than 30 days, and pro-rata refund of prepaid fees is tied to termination for Garman's default (§ 17(c)) rather than to a § 17(b) convenience exit. Noted in the rationale, not redlined.

No redline proposed.
